content.comment_body: I am considering installing [product_name] with [product_name] operator device in the engine room of a ship, where the maximum working temperature can reach 55°C. From the specifications, [product_name] operates in the 0–55°C range. Has anyone installed [product_name] on a ship before? I'm concerned about potential failures that could stop the ship unexpectedly. Perhaps I should consider another PLC such as [product_name] or an alternative? Additionally, regarding the electrical panel, I see that [company_name] Spacial series are certified for marine use. What are your thoughts? I read the [product_name] certificate and am wondering what 'Bridge and Deck zone' means—is that referring to the electric engine room? For reference, the document states: - [product_name] series with DC power supply meets EMC for Bridge and Deck Zone if a filter of type B84113-C or equivalent (C=2×0.47µF + 2×4700pF, L=4×4.7mH) is used. - [product_name] series with AC power supply also meets EMC requirements for Bridge and Deck Zone.

You can find certification details in the [product_name] manual. More information and certificates are available at [url]. Enter the order number for [product_name] and select 'certificates'. Any restrictions will be listed in the documentation.

We will use [product_name] for this solution because it provides a higher level of protection than [product_name] for our needs. The project involves converting an electric ship with two 750 HP electric motors.

Hello, I am an electrician and we have multiple [product_name] units installed onboard our vessels. Some are used in critical equipment like fuel treatment filters, starting air compressors, and ballast pumps. Most issues arise from aging units, like the [article_no] series we still operate, but the newer [article_no] series have been used for upgrades without major problems. If you use the 230V AC version, I recommend adding an extra varistor for protection against voltage spikes. We also have several [product_name] units installed as upgrades from MAN diesel in areas where the temperature sometimes reached 60°C, and these have operated without issues. If you plan on using a touch screen, install it in the control room, since they don't perform well at high temperatures.

analysis.insight_summary: Users discuss installing [product_name] devices in marine settings, focusing on temperature tolerance, certification for marine and EMC compliance, and system reliability. Concerns revolve around operating temperature limits and appropriateness for critical applications in high-temperature environments such as ship engine rooms. Experienced users indicate that [product_name] performs reliably in less critical roles, while more advanced PLC hardware such as [product_name] is preferred when increased protection is needed.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect hardware to be robust, certified for marine use, and able to tolerate high temperatures, with easy access to relevant certification documentation. Reliability in demanding shipboard conditions and possession of appropriate marine certifications are key requirements.
